paragraphs.title: The Flying Scroll and the Curse of Wrongdoing

answers: A woman sitting in an ephah
easy.q: What did the prophet see at the beginning of the vision?

answers: Twenty cubits long and ten cubits broad
easy.explanation: The roll was twenty cubits long and ten cubits broad.
easy.q: What were the dimensions of the roll?

answers: Thieves and those who swear falsely
easy.explanation: The curse enters the house of the thief and the house of him who swears falsely.
easy.q: Who was targeted by the curse?

answers: A curse going forth over the whole earth
A list of measurements for the temple
A message about building a new house
medium.explanation: The angel identified it as the curse going forth over the face of the whole earth.
medium.q: What did the flying roll represent?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes judgment against those who steal or swear falsely.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “cut off” mean in this passage?

answers: It remains there and consumes the house
medium.explanation: The curse remains in the house and consumes its timber and stones.
medium.q: What happens when the curse enters the sinner’s house?

answers: The roll only describes the houses from a distance
The curse from the roll enters and destroys the houses
The roll is made from the stones of the houses
challenge.explanation: The curse goes into the houses of thieves and those who swear falsely.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the flying roll and the houses of sinners?

answers: The vision addresses different kinds of wrongdoing
The vision concerns only the roll’s measurements
The vision separates wrongdoing from judgment
challenge.explanation: The passage names both stealing and swearing falsely as offenses under judgment.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the curse addresses both stealing and false swearing?

answers: The house is consumed, and then the roll appears
The prophet sees the roll, learns its meaning, and sees its effect on sinners’ houses
The prophet sees a house, and then an ephah is built inside it
challenge.explanation: The roll appears first, its purpose is explained, and its judgment on houses is described.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of events in the vision?

answers: A house in the land of Shinar
easy.explanation: The angel told Zechariah to see “what is this that goeth forth,” and identified it as an ephah.
easy.q: What did the angel show the prophet?

easy.explanation: A woman was sitting in the midst of the ephah.

medium.explanation: An ephah was a vessel used for measuring, and it is the object shown in the vision.

answers: It covered the mouth of the ephah
It marked the land of Shinar
medium.explanation: The weight of lead was cast upon the mouth of the ephah.
medium.q: What was the “talent of lead” used for?

answers: He cast her into the ephah and covered it with lead
medium.explanation: The angel cast wickedness into the ephah and placed the lead over its opening.
medium.q: What did the angel do to the woman in the ephah?

challenge.explanation: The angel explicitly interpreted the woman as wickedness.
challenge.q: What does the woman in the ephah symbolize?

answers: The ephah becomes a flying roll
challenge.explanation: The heavy lead covering depicts wickedness being shut inside the ephah.
challenge.q: What is the significance of covering the ephah with lead?

answers: A visible measure or representation of wickedness throughout the land
A hiding place that conceals all wrongdoing
A tool used only to measure wings
challenge.explanation: The ephah is presented as a representation seen throughout the earth, with wickedness identified inside it.
challenge.q: What does the ephah represent in the vision’s larger message?

paragraphs.title: The Ephah Carried to the Land of Shinar

easy.explanation: Zechariah saw two women come out and lift up the ephah.
easy.q: How many women carried the ephah?

easy.explanation: Their wings were like the wings of a stork.
easy.q: What were the women’s wings like?

easy.explanation: The angel said it would be taken to the land of Shinar.

answers: Between the earth and the heaven
Between the house and the city
Between the sea and the river
medium.explanation: They lifted the ephah between the earth and the heaven.
medium.q: Between what places did the women carry the ephah?

answers: Placed on its prepared foundation or stand
medium.explanation: The ephah would be established and placed on its own base.
medium.q: What does “set there upon her own base” mean?

answers: A house would be built for it, and it would be set on its base
It would be burned in heaven
medium.explanation: The angel said that a house would be built for it in Shinar, where it would be established.
medium.q: What would happen to the ephah in the land of Shinar?

answers: The removal or transfer of wickedness and the curse to Shinar
The spreading of blessing throughout the earth
The delivery of a measuring vessel to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The vision portrays wickedness being carried away to the land of Shinar.
challenge.q: What does the carrying of the ephah to Shinar represent in the vision?

answers: It was being transported by the winged women to its appointed destination
It remained permanently inside a house
It changed into a flying roll
challenge.explanation: The description emphasizes the supernatural transport of the ephah.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the ephah was carried between earth and heaven?

answers: The ephah is carried, brought to Shinar, and given a house and foundation
A house is built, then the ephah is created and confined
The roll reaches Shinar, and then the women make the ephah
challenge.explanation: The women carry the ephah to Shinar, where a house is built and it is placed on its base.
challenge.q: What is the correct sequence of the vision?
